facts.text: The accessible entrance is on Elm Street at the southeast side. South elevators serve every level, including the Ballroom; a north elevator also serves all levels.
quote: The ADA Accessibility entrance is located on the southeast side of the building on Elm Street. From here, you will enter the Western & Southern Lobby where you will find the Box Office and two South Elevators that provide easy access to every level of Music Hall, including the Ballroom. A North Concourse Elevator also serves all levels, including the Wilks Studio and Balcony Parlor.

facts.text: Access Ambassadors at the southeast entrance provide wayfinding and seat assistance; wheelchairs can be requested for transport from curb or lobby to seats.
quote: Access Ambassadors are available at the southeast entrance on Elm Street. These ambassadors will help you find your way and assist you to your seat. Wheelchairs are available upon request for guests needing assistance from the curb or lobby to their seats.

facts.text: Guest Services in the Lindner Grand Foyer provides assistive listening devices with a neck loop for T-coil users.
quote: Assistive Listening Devices designed to enhance the sound of performances for guests who are deaf or hard of hearing are available at Guest Services, located at the northeast corner of Music Hall's Lindner Grand Foyer. This new system uses Listen Technologies' next generation of personal listening devices, and its integrated neck loop/lanyard improves the listening experience for T-coil users.

facts.text: First-aid services are located in the North Concourse on the Orchestra level; ask staff for assistance.
quote: First Aid Services are available in the North Concourse on the Orchestra Level. For assistance, speak with Music Hall staff member.

facts.text: Special seating is available for guests who cannot transfer out of their wheelchairs or have other seating needs; contact the Box Office in advance when possible.
quote: Special seating is available for guests unable to transfer out of their wheelchairs or with other special seating needs. When possible, contact the Box Office in advance.

facts.text: Single-room restrooms are at the 1241 Elm Street entrance near the Box Office, on the north side of the Orchestra level, on the south side of the Balcony level and on the west side of the Ballroom.
quote: Single Unit Restrooms can be found at the following locations: 1241 Elm Street entrance, near the Box Office North side of the Orchestra level of Springer Auditorium South side of the Balcony level of Springer Auditorium West side of the Ballroom

facts.text: Bags are limited to 18 × 18 × 8 inches. Staff may make exceptions for medical necessity; notify a staff member. Visitors with concerns about screening with a pacemaker or metal implant may request another screening method.
quote: For your safety and expedited entry into the Aronoff Center or Music Hall, bag sizes are restricted to 18" x 18" x 8" . Bags exceeding this designated size will not be permitted inside the building. Exceptions can be made if you have a medical necessity. If so, notify a staff member who can assist you.
Is it safe for me to walk through the metal detectors if I have a pacemaker or a metal medical implant?
If you have any concerns, please speak with a staff member at Music Hall or the Aronoff Center, and we will be happy to screen you using another method.

facts.text: The drop-off lane is on Elm Street near the Box Office and wheelchair entrance at 1241 Elm Street. Music Hall does not own or manage the listed parking facilities, so confirm availability and rates with the operator.
quote: A convenient drop-off lane is located in front of Music Hall on Elm Street, near the Box Office and wheelchair-accessible entrance (1241 Elm Street). NOTE: Music Hall does not own or manage the parking facilities listed below. Parking rates are subject to change and are posted at each lot.

facts.text: For Springer Hall performances, staff can provide access to an area for nursing. Ask a staff member for its location and entry; this page does not describe equipment or a dedicated room available for every event.
quote: Our Springer Hall performances do offer an area for nursing mothers. Please speak to a staff member for assistance and access to the location.

facts.text: Music Hall’s access page asks visitors bringing a service animal to notify their ticketing representative when buying tickets and says animals should remain leashed or harnessed. Confirm any seating arrangements with the venue.
quote: Service animals are always welcome and should remain on a leash or in a harness at all times. If you plan to bring a service animal to an event, please notify your ticketing services representative at the time of purchase.

facts.text: Music Hall entry generally begins one to one-and-a-half hours before an event, depending on the performance’s policy. Anyone who leaves the building must repeat safety screening to re-enter.
quote: MUSIC HALL: You may enter Music Hall anytime beginning one to one-and-one-half hours before the start of an event, depending on the policies of the performance.
Anyone who leaves either building at any time will need to repeat the safety screening to re-enter the venues.

facts.text: The tours FAQ says no bathroom breaks are scheduled and recommends arriving 15 minutes early. Outdoor-tour guests are directed to Washington Park’s Race Street restroom because indoor Music Hall restrooms are not available for that tour.
quote: We do not stop at any restrooms or take any bathroom breaks during any of our tours. You are encouraged to arrive 15 minutes before your start time to use the restrooms. Outdoor building tour guests should visit the park's public restroom on the Race Street side of Washington Park as indoor restrooms will not be available.

facts.text: Indoor Music Hall tours offer brief opportunities to sit; tell the organizer when booking if minimal stairs would be a problem. Outdoor tours have no sitting opportunities and expect participants to remain on their feet without assistance. The FAQ also says tour paths accommodate walkers and wheelchairs; confirm your route and support needs.
quote: Indoor building tours provide some opportunities to sit briefly. Our indoor tour is completely ADA accessible however, please let us know at the time of your reservation if you have trouble climbing minimal stairs.

Our outdoor building tour is a 360 degree walk around the building which is about the length and width of a football field. The route does not go up or down any stairs or hills. Tour guests are expected to stay on their feet the whole time without assistance and there are no opportunities to sit along the tour route.
Cincinnati Music Hall is 100% ADA compliant and the tour path accommodates those in walkers and wheelchairs.

facts.text: The tours FAQ describes indoor tours year-round and outdoor tours May–October. It recommends advance tickets because spaces are limited; same-day purchase depends on space. Reservations must be paid for in advance. Confirm the current tour calendar before travelling.
quote: Indoor tours are offered year round while outdoor tours are only offered May - October. It is recommended that guests make a reservation and buy tickets in advance through the Cincinnati Arts Association or Music Hall box offices as space is limited. If space is available, tickets can be purchased the day of the tour. All reservations must be paid for in advance.

facts.text: Telescope eyepieces on the two main telescopes can be 4 to over 14 feet above the floor and usually require climbing a stepped platform.
quote: The eyepieces on our two main telescopes can be anywhere from 4 feet to over 14 feet above the floor, which typically requires climbing a stepped platform to reach.

facts.text: In the 1904 Mitchel building, a ramp leads to a side entrance on the main floor with the classroom, lobby and restrooms; its telescope dome room is reached only by 5 steps with handrails.
quote: There is an ADA compliant ramp to the side entrance which brings visitors into the main floor with access to the classroom, lobby, and restrooms.
The Telescope Dome Room is only accessible by 5 steps with handrails on both sides.

facts.text: The 1873 Herget building is temporarily closed for expansion. The same access page describes its dome as reached by 27 stairs and its existing lift as potentially unsuitable for motorized wheelchairs or extended leg rests. Those descriptions do not establish post-renovation access or current visitor entry.
quote: This building is temporarily closed as we bring you an exciting expansion of our exhibt space and more accessible facilities.
The lift may not be suitable for wheelchairs with leg rests extended or motorized wheelchairs.
The Telescope Dome Room is only accessible by stairs. A total of 27 stairs with 3 landings and one handrail.

facts.text: Level parking is directly next to both buildings; there are no marked spaces, but places can be reserved with cones or signage given notice.
quote: There is level parking directly adjacent to both buildings. While there are no marked parking places, with notice we can reserve places with cones or signage.

facts.text: Visitors needing assistance should say so when reserving or before visiting; depending on staffing and equipment, individualized tours and a portable telescope may be offered.
quote: If you need additional assistance please inform us when making reservations or before visiting. Depending on staffing and equipment available, staff and/or volunteers may be able offer individualized tours and use of a portable telescope for stargazing.

facts.text: The observatory's FAQ says it is currently open by appointment only.
quote: We are currently open by appointment only.

facts.text: The Observatory describes its main public areas as relatively level, with blacktop or brick paths and walkways. This does not establish a step-free route into the telescope rooms.
quote: The main public areas are relatively level and have blacktop or brick paths and walkways.

facts.text: The Observatory lists an outdoor drinking fountain and two benches, and describes two restrooms in the 1904 Mitchel building as accessible. It does not provide restroom dimensions or adult-changing details.
quote: There is an ADA compliant outdoor drinking fountain and two benches for seating.
The 1904 observatory houses our main classroom, original 1845 telescope, and two accessible restrooms.

facts.text: The observatory says it may not have staff with the skills to fully assist visitors with vision, hearing, physical or developmental disabilities.
quote: Due to our limited budget we do not necessarily have on-hand staff with the skills to fully assist vision, hearing or physically/developmentally impaired visitors.

facts.text: The Mitchel building’s front entrance has five steps with handrails. The published alternative is the side ramp to the main floor; reaching the dome and eyepiece involves additional steps.
quote: The front entrance has 5 steps with handrails. There is an ADA compliant ramp to the side entrance which brings visitors into the main floor with access to the classroom, lobby, and restrooms.
The Telescope Dome Room is only accessible by 5 steps with handrails on both sides. As noted above, reaching the telescope eyepiece usually involves additional steps.

facts.text: The directions page places on-site events in the smaller Mitchel building, on the right when entering the circle. It describes an uphill 0.3-mile walk from Metro Route 11, with the closest stop at Erie Avenue and St. Johns Avenue. Confirm current service and the walking route with Metro and the Observatory.
quote: Onsite events will take place in the smaller building (Mitchel) on your right when you enter the circle.

Although we are not directly along a Cincinnati Metro route, you can find us a short, uphill .3 mile walk off the #11 bus. The bus runs 24/7 and the closest stop to the Observatory is Erie Ave. and St. Johns Ave.

facts.text: The renovation page says the Herget building, Clark telescope and museum spaces are unavailable during work that began in July 2026, while Mitchel building programming continues. New restroom facilities are a project objective, not evidence of completed facilities or a reopening date.
quote: Beginning July 2026, the Cincinnati Observatory is entering A New Phase, a comprehensive campaign that includes a renovation of our Herget building!
Installation of ADA compliant restroom facilities

While the Herget building, Clark telescope and museum spaces will be unavailable as the work is completed, we can't wait to share the incredible end result. Our Mitchel building will remain open, as will access to our Mitchel telescope, the oldest public telescope still available for viewing in this hemisphere!

facts.text: Wheelchair seating is offered in both theaters, and the Rouse Theatre also has transfer seats. These places are subject to availability and should be requested when reserving tickets.
quote: The Playhouse is fully equipped to accommodate patrons with mobility impairments in both theatres. In addition, transfer seats are available in Moe and Jack's Place - The Rouse Theatre. Accessible seating for wheelchairs and transfer seats are subject to availability and should be requested at the time of ticket reservation.

facts.text: Both theaters use hearing loops compatible with T-coil devices and offer hearing-enhancement receivers. Large-print programs are available from ushers.
quote: Moe and Jack's Place - The Rouse Theatre and the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre both have a hearing loop system which works with existing T-Coil or Telecoil enabled hearing aids or cochlear implants. In addition, hearing enhancement receivers providing volume enhancement to patrons with hearing impairment are available. Please see the house manager for more information.
Large print programs are available upon request from the ushers.

facts.text: Selected sensory-friendly/relaxed performances accommodate visitors who benefit from a more relaxed setting; check the performance calendar.
quote: Our sensory-friendly/relaxed performance is designed for anyone who would benefit from a more sensory-aware and relaxed theatre experience. Although open to all, these performances are offered to accommodate individuals with sensory sensitivities, anxiety, dementia, autism spectrum disorders, learning differences or challenges, and others who need a more accommodating environment.

facts.text: ASL and audio description are offered on designated performance dates.
quote: Audio-described and ASL signed performances
Signed performances for those with hearing impairments are offered for designated performances. Please see dates below.

Audio-Described Performances The Playhouse was the first theatre in Ohio to offer regularly scheduled audio description for the visually impaired. Trained volunteers describe the visual elements of the production via a hearing enhancement system, allowing patrons to hear dialogue, music and other sound effects. The description is timed to avoid interfering with dialogue. Before the show and during intermission, show and actor information are shared. This service is free. Please see dates below. 26-27 season performance dates:

facts.text: A curbside drop-off gives direct access to the street-level Box Office, lobby and elevator.
quote: A curbside drop-off area offers direct access to the street level Box Office, lobby and elevator to the second level.

facts.text: Accessible parking is in the Playhouse garage, is limited, and must be reserved and paid for in advance. Vehicles using these spaces must display a valid disability placard.
quote: Parking for those with disabilities is located in the Playhouse parking garage. Parking for persons with disabilities is limited and must be reserved and paid for in advance. All vehicles using these spaces must display a valid disability placard.

facts.text: The Rouse Theatre (Moe and Jack's Place) has accessible seating in every section, and its elevator goes up to the balcony or down to the front rows of the orchestra.
quote: Moe and Jack's Place features more legroom and better chairs, and accessible seating in every section! The elevator for the new building will take patrons up to the balcony or down to the front rows of the orchestra section.

facts.text: Deaf, hard-of-hearing, deafblind or speech-disabled patrons can dial 711 to reach the Box Office through Ohio Relay.
quote: Patrons who are deaf, hard-of-hearing, deafblind or speech disabled: Dial 711 to connect to our Box Office at 513-421-3888 via Ohio Relay services.

facts.text: The Rouse Theatre doors are on the first lobby level. The elevator serves the balcony and front orchestra rows, and also reaches the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre on the second floor. Arrange a specific seat and route when booking.
quote: The doors are on the first level of the lobby, which means that all patrons can access the new theatre on the same level where they enter the building, only using the elevator for seats in the balcony section or front rows. The elevator can also be used to access the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre, which will remain in its second-floor location.
The elevator for the new building will take patrons up to the balcony or down to the front rows of the orchestra section.

facts.text: For hearing-enhancement receivers, the Playhouse directs visitors to the house manager. Both theaters have hearing loops for T-coil or Telecoil hearing aids and cochlear implants; confirm how to collect and use any receiver you need.
quote: Moe and Jack's Place - The Rouse Theatre and the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre both have a hearing loop system which works with existing T-Coil or Telecoil enabled hearing aids or cochlear implants. In addition, hearing enhancement receivers providing volume enhancement to patrons with hearing impairment are available. Please see the house manager for more information.

facts.text: Audio description is free on the listed performance dates. Trained volunteers describe visual action through the hearing-enhancement system, avoiding dialogue; show and actor information is also shared before the performance and at intermission.
quote: Trained volunteers describe the visual elements of the production via a hearing enhancement system, allowing patrons to hear dialogue, music and other sound effects. The description is timed to avoid interfering with dialogue. Before the show and during intermission, show and actor information are shared. This service is free. Please see dates below.

facts.text: For the advertised relaxed performance of A Christmas Carol on November 28, 2026, the Playhouse describes reduced loud sound and strobe/strong-light effects, dimmed house lights, standing/movement areas, permitted exit and re-entry, and a lobby quiet space. Reduced effects do not mean no flashing lights.
quote: Minor adjustments to sensory elements of the production, such as lowering loud sounds and the reduction of strobe lights/strong lighting effects. House lights on but dimmed throughout the performance. Limited and socially distanced seating options and designated areas within the theatre for standing and moving around. Guests are welcome to exit and re-enter the theatre and to talk and express themselves vocally anytime during the performance. Designated quiet space in the lobby.
Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026, 12 p.m.

facts.text: For that November 28, 2026 relaxed A Christmas Carol performance, online orders are limited to six tickets; larger orders must be made by phone to arrange socially distanced seating. The page excludes children under five and gives a running time of one hour 50 minutes including a 20-minute interval; confirm details for your visit.
quote: Children under 5 are not admitted due to the full-length nature of the performance, which runs 1 hour and 50 minutes, including a 20-minute intermission.

Online, you can purchase up to six tickets. Tickets can also be purchased by calling our Box Office at 513-421-3888. Orders for more than six tickets must be made by phone to ensure socially distanced seating.
Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026, 12 p.m.

facts.text: The relaxed-performance page says an Audience Guide is provided digitally to ticket holders seven days before the performance. Ask for the guide for your selected show.
quote: An Audience Guide will be provided in advance and distributed digitally to all ticket holders seven days prior to the performance.

facts.text: Both sets of entrance doors have push buttons for independent entry and exit, and an elevator connects the floors.
quote: Both entrances to the building (the interior and exterior doors of the vestibule) have the push buttons to allow for independent entrance/exit.
Our elevator provides access between floors.

facts.text: All studios are accessible for guests using mobility devices, and the Sheakley Premier Performance Studio and the Community Terrace and Performance Plaza can seat people using mobility devices.
quote: All of the studios at the Center for Dance are accessible for guests using mobility devices. Both the Sheakley Premier Performance Studio and the Community Terrace and Performance Plaza can accommodate seating for all people using a mobility device.

facts.text: The Ballet places designated accessible parking on the west (I-71) side near an entrance to the Center for Dance.
quote: Designated accessible parking is available on the west side (I-71 side) near the ground for entrance to the Center for Dance.

facts.text: All restrooms have accessible stalls, and the first-level restroom and locker facilities include an accessible shower stall.
quote: All restrooms throughout the Center for Dance have accessible stalls for guests with specific needs. Both restroom and locker facilities on the first level of the Center for Dance have shower stalls that are accessible for guests using mobility devices.

facts.text: Cincinnati Ballet presents sensory-friendly versions of select ballets during the season; check where each one is performed.
quote: Cincinnati Ballet presents a sensory-friendly version of select ballets throughout the season.

facts.text: For CB Moves for Parkinson's classes, the accessible entrance is the Craig and Anne Maier Artistic Entrance; use the call button. Classes run three times a week on a drop-in basis.
quote: Classes are offered three times per week and are available on a drop-in basis so there's no advance commitment required.
The accessible entrance is the Craig and Anne Maier Artistic Entrance. Please use the call button for secure entry.

facts.text: At sensory-friendly ballets you can come and go from the theater as you please.
quote: Entry and exit to the theater is not restricted. You may come and go as you please.

facts.text: The Ballet identifies an Everybody Restroom on the first floor with a shower stall it describes as accessible. It does not specify an adult changing table or transfer equipment.
quote: The Everybody Restroom on the first floor is both accessible and includes a shower stall that is accessible.

facts.text: For CB Moves for Parkinson’s, visitors signing up in person are asked to arrive 15 minutes early for check-in and waivers. The online schedule links to Mindbody for reservations, payment and schedule or capacity changes.
quote: The schedule below updates regularly and offers direct access to Cincinnati Ballet's Mindbody site. Through Mindbody you can: Reserve your space in class Purchase a class Create and manage your account Check changes to the schedule or class capacities If you prefer to sign-up in person, please arrive 15 minutes early to check in and complete any waivers prior to class.

facts.text: CB Moves for Parkinson’s costs $10 per class and includes a companion participant at no additional charge. Confirm the current class schedule and space before travelling.
quote: All classes are $10 and include a companion participant (if desired) at no additional charge.

facts.text: CB Moves for Parkinson’s participants may dance seated, use a chair or barre for balance, modify steps and take breaks. Standing and unaided movement across the floor are not required; this is class participation guidance, not a promise of transfer or personal-care assistance.
quote: At any point, dancers may opt to use a chair or the barre for balance instead of standing on their own, or to sit down in a chair and dance seated. Additionally, dancers are encouraged to modify steps as necessary to participate at their own level, and take breaks as needed. Standing and unaided movement across the floor is not necessary to participate. We have had many students successfully navigate class using wheelchairs, walkers, canes, and other mobility devices.

facts.text: For the Ballet’s sensory-friendly performances, house lights remain at half brightness, volunteers are stationed in the audience, lobby and outside, and quiet areas are designated in the lobby. Confirm the performance location; this is not an everyday quiet-room promise at the Center for Dance.
quote: House lights remain at half brightness during the entire performance.
Volunteers are stationed throughout the audience, lobby and outside the venue to assist audience members. Quiet areas are designated in the lobby.

facts.text: The JCC lists accessible parking, push-button door openers at the entrance and first-floor bathrooms, and elevator access to all floors. It does not give parking-space locations, door widths or a measured continuous route.
quote: Our building features accessible parking, push button door openers on the entrance and the first-floor bathrooms, and elevator access to all floors.

facts.text: The family locker room provides space for assistance with changing or showering. The JCC explicitly says it does not currently have adult changing tables; confirm any transfer or personal-care arrangements before visiting.
quote: We have a family locker room that allow space to assist with changing ( please note we do not currently have adult changing tables ) or showering as needed.

facts.text: Sensory kits with noise-reducing headphones, fidgets and other sensory items can be requested at the Welcome Desk. The FAQ says members and guests may borrow sensory bags from the front desk; availability is not quantified.
quote: Our sensory kits are equipped with noise-reducing headphones, a variety of fidgets, and other sensory items to meet the diverse needs of our guests. Request to borrow a Sensory Kit at the Welcome Desk
Sensory bags are available for members and guests to borrow from the front desk for members needing assistance managing their sensory needs while enjoying community programming at the J.

facts.text: The J Cafe offers Braille menus on request. A 3D-printed QR code at the register links to a plain-text online menu.
quote: The J Cafe offers braille menus upon request for customers to use. There is also a 3D-printed QR code that sits on the J Cafe register for customers to scan and access a plain-text menu online.

facts.text: To request an event accommodation, contact the program staff listed on its JLive registration or website page. If contact information is missing or the question is more detailed, the inclusion team can help; its published phone is 513-644-0713.
quote: If you are attending a program at the JCC and need an accommodation to participate, please email the staff member listed as the contact for that program. You can find their contact information on the JLive registration or website page related to the program. If you do not see contact information or have a more detailed question, please email [email protected] to connect with the Inclusion Coordinator.
Please reach out to our Inclusion department via the web form below, phone at 513.644.0713

facts.text: Examples of accommodations that visitors can discuss include ASL interpreting, captioning, sensory bags, reserved seating and social narratives or advance event agendas. These are request options, not a guarantee that each service is available for every program.
quote: Some examples of common accommodations are: ASL interpreting or captioning, use of sensory bags, reserved seating, and a social narrative or early access to the event agenda.
We encourage you to contact us to discuss your accessibility needs and supports needed to ensure your participation in JCC programs.

facts.text: For off-site programs, the JCC works within the host venue’s policies and capabilities and says it cannot guarantee every accommodation request. Check the registration page and contact the listed program staff about the specific location.
quote: Registration pages for all JCC events, on or off-site, should include information about any universal accessibility features available at the location such as parking and elevator access. When renting a space, we work within the policies and capabilities of the space and therefore cannot guarantee all accommodation requests will be fulfilled.
If you have questions about the accessibility of an event or need to request an accommodation, please reach out to the listed staff or email our Inclusion Coordinator

facts.text: The Fitness & Friends and Adapted Basketball descriptions expect participants to engage independently or with their own personal-care assistant. Adapted Total Body Workout similarly expects independent participation or help from the participant’s own direct-support professional; do not assume personal care is supplied.
quote: FITNESS & FRIENDS Ages 16+ Sundays, 1 - 3pm J Members: FREE | Public: $25 This engaging adaptive class offers low-impact exercise, socializing, and creative crafts. Participants should be able to engage independently or with the help of their own personal care assistant.

ADAPTED BASKETBALL Ages 18+ Every Other Thursday, 7 - 8pm J Members: FREE | Public: $25 In this exciting, team-focused exercise class, participants will work on basketball fundamentals while socializing and being active. Participants should be able to engage independently or with the help of their own personal care assistant.

ADAPTED TOTAL BODY WORKOUT Age 16+ Wednesdays, 7 - 8pm J Members: FREE | Public: $25 This inclusive adapted workout combines cardio and strength training in a circuit format, with stretching and yoga for a total body workout. Participants should be able to engage independently or with the help of their own direct support professional.

facts.text: The inclusion page links visual preparation guides for the JCC locker rooms, private swim lessons, theater visits and selected programs. Use the guide for the actual program and check its date; off-site guides describe other venues.
quote: Please click the links below for specific Social Narratives: Arts & Culture Events at the JCC What to Expect at the Oy Vey 5K What to Expect at the Theatre What to Expect at the Fall Market What to Expect for Jewish Community Night at the Cincinnati Cyclones Specific Cincinnati Cyclones Social Narrative Youth Programming What to Expect at Camp at the J What to Expect at Camp at the J: Swim What to Expect at Camp at the J: Shabbat What to Expect at Camp at the J: Field Trips What to Expect: Pokémon Club Swimming at the JCC All About the JCC Locker Rooms What to Expect at Private Swim Lessons

facts.text: The locker-room photo narrative describes touching a blue JCC fob to the black reader beside the door. If the door will not open, it directs visitors to the Welcome Desk for help. Confirm the entry arrangements for your membership or guest visit.
quote: To enter the locker room, I will touch my blue JCC fob to the black, rectangular pad next to the door.
If the locker room door won’t open, I should go back to the Welcome Desk and ask for help.

facts.text: In the locker-room narrative’s stair-based approach, the family locker room is first on the left, the men’s is second, and the women’s is at the end of the hall. The guide does not map an elevator approach; ask staff for the route that avoids stairs.
quote: To find the locker rooms, I will walk straight through the security gates and go down the stairs.
At the bottom of the stairs, I will go straight.
The family locker room is first on the left, the men’s is second, and the women’s is at the end of the hall.

facts.text: The private swim-lesson narrative warns that the pool can be loud with other users, including talking, yelling, laughter and lifeguard whistles. It says visitors may ask for a break in a quiet place; it does not identify a permanently quiet poolside room.
quote: The pool might be loud if there are other people using the space while I am there. I might hear talking, yelling, laughing, or even a lifeguard blowing a whistle.
If it feels too loud, I can try wearing headphones or ask for a break in a quiet place.

facts.text: Some vehicles in the JCC’s senior-transport fleet have wheelchair lifts; the operator asks riders to specify that need. Confirm the assigned vehicle, equipment limits and any boarding or personal assistance before booking.
quote: Our fleet of vehicles provide comfortable transportation and some include wheelchair lifts (please specify if you will need this service).

facts.text: The JCC describes weekday home pickup and return for seniors attending its activities, wellness programs, trips and lunches. This is a senior-program service, not a general public route; confirm eligibility, fares and booking notice.
quote: We provide daily transportation for seniors to visit the JCC. Every weekday, seniors are picked up at their homes and transported to the J for fun activities, wellness programs, trips, and lunches, and then returned home.

facts.text: The listed senior-transport areas are Amberley Village, Blue Ash, Deer Park, Golf Manor, Hyde Park, Kennedy Heights, Kenwood, Loveland, Mason, Montgomery, Pleasant Ridge, Reading, Roselawn, Silverton and Wyoming. Call 513-792-5667 to ask about pickup or an unlisted area; service beyond the list is not promised.
quote: Areas we currently serve include: Amberley Village, BlueAsh, Deer Park, Golf Manor, Hyde Park, Kennedy Heights, Kenwood, Loveland, Mason, Montgomery, Pleasant Ridge, Reading, Roselawn, Silverton, and Wyoming. Don't see your area on our list? Contact us to see if transportation can be arranged. For more information and to schedule a pickup, call: 513.792.5667

facts.text: The 60 & Better Center page identifies adults aged 60 and older as eligible for transportation and other senior services and describes pickup for members. It lists annual center dues of $50 per individual or $90 per household couple. These are center membership dues, not a quoted trip fare; confirm transport enrollment and charges.
quote: Adults ages 60 & Better are also eligible to receive cost effective meals, transportation services, Meals on Wheels, Shalom Phone telephone reassurance, and much more.
Annual membership dues are $50 per individual and $90 per household couple.
No transportation? No problem! We'll pick our members up, so they don't miss a thing!
